batch_strategy: Resolve the newly exposed m177 completion regime and conditional loading effects, then test specific remaining solvent-response extrema and fill informative gaps in molecular curves. Controlled comparisons use existing labels wherever possible. Selection emphasizes relationships that can generalize across remaining rows, with explicit allowance for same-tuple variability.

choices.reason: m177 at 10/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 6.08/45.29 mL. Measured 50-uL anchors aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58 at 20/1 and 5b706e17e8412d02342f at 50/1 finished at 8.50 and 59.88 mL. This intermediate condition tests whether the current prediction has transferred the 150-uL tail too broadly or whether the low-loading curve itself is strongly nonmonotonic.

m177 at 10/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 5.87/45.33 mL, almost matching the selected 50-uL prediction. Its measured 100-uL 50/1 anchor 4862e2fb71344ce16021 finished at only 7.31 mL, whereas aef5cafc63ca445e92fa at 150 uL and 10/1 finished at 46.72 mL. This directly tests the loading boundary of the newly learned late regime.

m177 at 5/1 and 100 uL, predicted 2.14/26.78 mL, pairs with the selected 10/1 condition. Existing 100-uL 1/1 and 2/1 labels 61764a2e9f71f1caa18e and bd76c7bdcd3681374617 are ordinary. The label locates the proposed completion increase and tests the predicted onset minimum independently of completion.

m125 in pure EA at 50 uL with a 500-uL DCM plug is predicted at 5.34/12.48 mL. It changes only plug volume relative to measured 300-uL row 55f2352b50967352163e, 4.87/12.85 mL. This economical matched comparison tests whether the repeated 1/1 plug association disappears at the strongest-eluent boundary.

This tests low-loading transfer and whether fitting larger-plug labels continues to displace the smaller-plug curve.

m92 at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 9.43/21.78 mL. The 100-uL 1/1 completion peak in e93e08d6bc42e91e2679 did not extend to 150 uL in 4451265787d29526a93a. With the selected 150-uL companion and existing 50-uL 5/1 observations, this tests whether that peak is confined to the strongest mixed-eluent conditions.

Its measured 150-uL 1/1 and 2/1 completions were 9.73 and 12.54 mL in 4451265787d29526a93a and f7cc49c21fea55ed9087. This extends a controlled loading-by-ratio comparison without assuming a universal amount direction.

m75 at 10/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 8.25/19.22 mL. The same loading at 50/1 finished at 11.63 mL in 28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e, while recent 150-uL 10/1 row dea5f0228035f44dd102 remained ordinary at 19.52 mL. This tests whether the weak-end decrease is localized and supplies a matched-ratio loading contrast to the 100- and 150-uL anchors.

m15 at 1/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 8.43/11.39 mL, with onset later than measured 10/1 row a41b395c8efbc1de1aa7, 5.50/8.99 mL. Together with the selected 5/1 point and measured pure-EA baseline 4fc25128f65d2cf6e786, this tests a substantial predicted strong-side maximum in cyclohexyl acrylate.

m15 at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 4.70/9.43 mL. Its controlled pairing with the selected 1/1 row distinguishes a real local maximum from an interpolation artifact, while the measured 10/1 anchor a41b395c8efbc1de1aa7 constrains the weaker side. This curve can inform other acrylate rows rather than transferring a generic ester correction.

m17 at 1/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 8.54/12.20 mL, substantially later than its selected 2/1 prediction. Existing m17 labels d1ec836ef828ebbf94ad and 946f712a81f3990f568f cover weaker eluents, not this proposed maximum. This tests whether the acrylate strong-side shape extends to a trifluoroethyl substituent.

m17 at 2/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 4.08/7.20 mL. The selected 1/1 companion holds every loading variable fixed, making the large predicted decrease directly testable. These two labels constrain an uncovered portion of the curve and discriminate solvent-response structure from transfer of the m15 prediction pattern.

m91 at 1/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 8.83/13.13 mL, versus measured 2/1 row 02ddeed8a16d3adf3e28 at 5.79/9.17 mL. This tests another specific strong-side maximum, now in an acetylenic diester. Its two ester groups do not establish a late response: measured 20/1 row 93f10a8edf06f7acae26 also remains ordinary.

m91 at 5/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 5.04/7.99 mL, below both the selected 1/1 prediction and measured 2/1 completion in 02ddeed8a16d3adf3e28. The controlled pair tests the depth and location of this proposed minimum and helps distinguish the diester response from the flat m80 and more retained m75 curves.

m77 at 2/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 11.49/14.95 mL. Its 150-uL observation 308ffc82485e086c1c09 had nearly coincident endpoints, 13.69/13.72 mL. Measuring another amount tests whether the high-onset branch transfers or reflects a localized observation, and adds coverage for a bromoester with few supplied measured anchors.

m130 in pure EA at 100 uL is predicted at 6.01/11.72 mL, later at both endpoints than measured 2/1 row 2bd50654bad989d82c87, 4.62/7.92 mL. This tests a strong-eluent reversal in a neutral aromatic nitrile and supplies a baseline distinct from the well-established weak-eluent curves of halobenzonitriles.

m60 in pure EA at 100 uL is predicted at 4.96/8.82 mL. Measured 5/1 row 62d7ea74ab73fa6214b4 is much later at 19.65/34.70 mL. This strongest-eluent anchor, paired with the selected 2/1 condition, tests how a secondary alcohol separated from the phenyl ring enters the retained regime.

m60 at 2/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 11.04/18.52 mL. With its selected pure-EA baseline and measured 5/1 row 62d7ea74ab73fa6214b4, this tests the predicted rising curve. The related m61 instead has measured completion decreasing from 2/1 to 5/1, so transferring its benzylic-alcohol response is an untested assumption.

m184 at 50/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 7.32/22.32 mL and lies at high CW distance. Its measured 10/1 anchor e78030609295a056f86f is 5.04/13.80 mL. This tests weak-eluent growth for a carbonyl flanked by two bromines, a useful structural boundary relative to the more retained difluoroaldehyde in c32500e81a05cfd2273d and the early-onset mixed-halogen aldehydes.

m179 at 20/1 and 100 uL is predicted at 9.06/25.03 mL. Matching-loading observations b6dc1ec0dbd724128ce3 at 10/1 and a36291cab664852df5e5 at 50/1 bracket a completion rise from 18.62 to 36.28 mL. m38 at 2/1 and 50 uL is predicted at 5.79/15.72 mL. With the selected 5/1 point, this fills the onset of retention growth between measured 100-uL 1/1 and 10/1 anchors 0537c303027eef12ba09 and 8e4d62928039d2200288. hypotheses.content: m125 has a repeatable association between a larger DCM loading plug and later completion at 1/1 across 100 and 150 uL samples, while its smaller-plug 2/1 completion is nearly stable across the measured amounts. The association is conditional: m168 and m88 do not support universal plug broadening, and m125 onset direction differs by configuration.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Current predictions remain almost invariant to plug changes and can mix distinct recorded configurations. Boundary labels can teach conditional interactions while limiting transfer to unrelated scaffolds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m125 plug association vanish in pure EA, and does the smaller-plug 1/1 completion remain near 20 mL at 50 uL?

hypotheses.content: m177 has a measured late-completion series at 150 uL from 10/1 through 50/1, and late completion also occurs at 50 uL and 50/1. Thus the tail is neither uniformly absent nor restricted to high loading. The early 100-uL 50/1 and 50-uL 20/1 observations leave competing explanations involving conditional response, variability or unrecorded differences.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest acquisition errors reveal a major completion failure, but indiscriminate tail transfer would conflict with measured configurations. Intermediate labels can constrain amount-by-ratio response and onset/completion decoupling.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the newly predicted late 10/1 completions reproduced at 50 and 100 uL, and where does the 100-uL curve leave its ordinary strong-eluent regime?

hypotheses.content: The apparent loading patterns in m92 and m75 may be confined to particular ratios. The m92 100-uL completion peak at 1/1 does not imply monotonic loading dependence or a transferable 1/1-to-2/1 decrease. The m75 50/1 loading contrast also does not extend automatically to 10/1. Variability remains an alternative to deterministic interactions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Predicted loading responses are often nearly flat, but fitting every contrast as a smooth amount effect risks learning spurious corrections. Local extensions test the boundaries of the observed differences.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does a 100-uL completion peak persist for m92 at 5/1, and is m75 at 50 uL ordinary at 10/1 despite its earlier 50/1 completion?

hypotheses.content: Some remaining predicted maxima, minima and compressed elution intervals may be interpolation artifacts. Recent measurements rejected several specific extrema, but measured fluorenone behavior shows that a universal monotonic solvent-response correction would also be inappropriate. Each proposed shape requires endpoint-specific evidence.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These failures affect ordinary-retention rows and can persist despite small or crossing quantile spreads. Controlled pairs and measured neighboring conditions can constrain graph-condition interpolation without erasing real curvature.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which proposed acrylate and diester maxima, methylated-ketone baseline decreases, m127 onset maximum and m155 minimum survive measurement, and does the m48 weak-eluent decrease occur?

hypotheses.content: The m61 early-onset observation at 10/1 is localized with respect to loading: its 50-uL onset is substantially later than its 100-uL onset, although completion is similar. Its measured completion dip from 2/1 to 5/1 should therefore not be transferred automatically to m60, whose OH group has a different structural relationship to the phenyl ring.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Alcohol similarity alone does not specify the joint onset/completion curve. Anchoring m60 at strong and intermediate eluent strength tests structural transfer beyond the unusual m61 branch.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m60 follow the predicted rising pure-EA-to-2/1-to-5/1 curve under fixed recorded loading?

hypotheses.content: Substantial completion variability occurs at identical recorded m104 tuples at both 10/1 and 20/1. A deterministic sample-amount explanation cannot account for those within-tuple differences. This is measured evidence for caution when interpreting other sparse loading contrasts causally.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Forcing the predictor to explain every observed difference through recorded loading could create incorrect interactions. The batch prioritizes new discriminating conditions over further m104 repeats now that variability is established at two ratios.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the additional m177 and m92 local series show coherent conditional patterns, or further contradictions that limit deterministic interpretation?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes strengthen the need for conditional failure repair. For m177, 150-uL completion increased through 46.72, 57.02 and 81.30 mL at 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1, while the new 50-uL 50/1 result finished at 59.88 mL. These outcomes reject both uniformly early behavior and a tail restricted to high loading. The measured early 100-uL 50/1 and 50-uL 20/1 anchors still prevent a simple global correction; the selected intermediate conditions test the current transfer directly. For m125, the 150-uL 1/1 plug contrast reproduced the large completion difference, and the smaller-plug 2/1 result remained near 29.5 mL at 50 uL. Conversely, m168 at 10/1 and the pure-EA m88 pair showed much smaller completion contrasts, narrowing the plug hypothesis further. The new m92 150-uL labels reversed the earlier proposed cross-loading ratio shape: completion increased from 1/1 to 2/1 rather than decreasing. The m75 150-uL 10/1 label was ordinary, limiting transfer of its weak-eluent loading contrast. The m104 10/1 repeat differed from its earlier identical tuple by about 9.65 mL in completion, paralleling the roughly 10 mL difference at 20/1; the earlier deterministic amount explanation is no longer tenable as a complete account. The m61 50-uL onset of 11.11 mL did not reproduce the 100-uL early onset of 3.04 mL, so I shift the alcohol question toward structural and loading boundaries. Several proposed maxima or compressed predictions in m110, m87, m129, m123, m85, m71 and m155 were not reproduced. The accurate tetralone pair and reasonably captured nitrile and boronic-ester points reduce the value of extending those already anchored conditions. Benzyl acrylate did grow at weak eluent, but much less than predicted. These are historical acquisition errors and measured contrasts, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines targeted repair with tests of relationships that remain poorly constrained across the eligible rows. The m177 series challenges a large, newly exposed completion failure while preserving the early measured exceptions. The m125 and m92 comparisons test recorded configuration interactions with existing controls; m75 and m77 probe boundaries where apparent loading effects could instead reflect localized observations or variability. The response-shape experiments address recurring errors in ordinary-retention regions: matched pairs test specific predicted extrema in acrylates, an acetylenic diester, methylated acetophenones and an ortho-methoxy ketone. Single points use measured neighboring conditions to test remaining minima or baseline reversals. The m60 pair explores a chemically meaningful alcohol transfer boundary. The dibromoaldehyde, cyclic ketone, acetylfluorene and dioxole-ketone selections fill gaps in established molecular curves where functional-group environment and recorded configuration can alter transfer. Multiple rows for a molecule form interpretable local experiments; duplicate catalog IDs for the same unmeasured tuple were otherwise avoided. Cross-molecule comparisons retain differences in density, amount, solvent and plug volume. Quantile spreads are treated as single-predictor behavior, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and V2 minus V1 remains the physical elution interval. All 32 distinct IDs and their supplied unrounded premeasurement predictions are fixed together, with no pending experiments or additional label reveals. Numerical predictions in reasons are rounded only for readability.
